\section{Installation}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/installation:installation}}\label{\detokenize{user-guide/installation::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This guide covers how to install and set up 5e2pdf on your system.


\subsection{Requirements}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/installation:requirements}}\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Python 3.11 or higher

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
LaTeX distribution (for PDF compilation)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Git (for cloning 5etools data)

\end{itemize}


\subsection{Python Installation}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/installation:python-installation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
5e2pdf requires Python 3.11 or higher. You can download Python from the official website:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxurl{https://www.python.org/downloads/}


\subsection{Installing 5e2pdf}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/installation:installing-5e2pdf}}

\subsubsection{Via pip (Recommended)}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/installation:via-pip-recommended}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }5e2pdf
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{From Source}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/installation:from-source}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
git\PYG{+w}{ }clone\PYG{+w}{ }https://github.com/your\PYGZhy{}repo/5e2pdf.git
\PYG{n+nb}{cd}\PYG{+w}{ }5e2pdf
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}e\PYG{+w}{ }.
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{LaTeX Installation}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/installation:latex-installation}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For PDF compilation, you’ll need a LaTeX distribution with XeLaTeX support.


\subsubsection{macOS}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/installation:macos}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Using Homebrew}
brew\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}cask\PYG{+w}{ }mactex

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Or using MacPorts}
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }port\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }texlive\PYGZhy{}xetex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Ubuntu/Debian}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/installation:ubuntu-debian}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }apt\PYGZhy{}get\PYG{+w}{ }update
sudo\PYG{+w}{ }apt\PYGZhy{}get\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }texlive\PYGZhy{}xetex\PYG{+w}{ }texlive\PYGZhy{}fonts\PYGZhy{}recommended
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsubsection{Windows}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/installation:windows}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Download and install MiKTeX from:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxurl{https://miktex.org/download}


\subsection{Setting Up Data Sources}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/installation:setting-up-data-sources}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
5e2pdf works with JSON data from the 5etools project. You’ll need to clone their data repository:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Clone the 5etools data repository}
git\PYG{+w}{ }clone\PYG{+w}{ }https://github.com/5etools\PYGZhy{}mirror\PYGZhy{}3/5etools\PYGZhy{}src.git

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Create a symlink to the data directory}
ln\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}s\PYG{+w}{ }../5etools\PYGZhy{}src/data\PYG{+w}{ }data
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Alternatively, you can specify custom data paths in your configuration.


\subsection{Verification}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/installation:verification}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
To verify your installation, run:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
5e2pdf\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}version
5e2pdf\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}help
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You should see version information and help text if everything is installed correctly.


\subsection{Configuration}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/installation:configuration}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
5e2pdf uses a configuration file for default settings. You can create one at:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Linux/macOS: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\textasciitilde{}/.config/5e2pdf/config.yaml}}

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Windows: \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\%APPDATA\%\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}5e2pdf\textbackslash{}\textbackslash{}config.yaml}}

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Example configuration:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{n+nt}{data\PYGZus{}paths}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{p+pIndicator}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{./data}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{p+pIndicator}{\PYGZhy{}}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{./homebrew}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{n+nt}{output}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{default\PYGZus{}directory}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{./output}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{include\PYGZus{}images}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{false}

\PYG{n+nt}{latex}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{engine}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{xelatex}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{additional\PYGZus{}packages}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{p+pIndicator}{[}\PYG{p+pIndicator}{]}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Troubleshooting}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/installation:troubleshooting}}

\subsubsection{Common Issues}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/installation:common-issues}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{ImportError: No module named ‘pydantic’}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This usually means the installation didn’t complete properly. Try:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
pip\PYG{+w}{ }install\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}upgrade\PYG{+w}{ }5e2pdf
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{LaTeX compilation fails}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Make sure you have XeLaTeX installed and available in your PATH:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
which\PYG{+w}{ }xelatex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{No data found}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Ensure you’ve cloned the 5etools data repository and created the symlink:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
ls\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}la\PYG{+w}{ }data/
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
You should see directories like \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{adventure/}}, \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{book/}}, etc.

\section{Quick Start Guide}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/quickstart:quick-start-guide}}\label{\detokenize{user-guide/quickstart::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This guide will get you up and running with 5e2pdf in just a few minutes.


\subsection{Your First Conversion}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/quickstart:your-first-conversion}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Let’s start by converting a simple spell or item file to LaTeX:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Quick convert a JSON file to LaTeX}
5e2pdf\PYG{+w}{ }quick\PYG{+w}{ }spells.json\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}output\PYG{+w}{ }spells.tex

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert and compile to PDF in one step}
5e2pdf\PYG{+w}{ }quick\PYG{+w}{ }spells.json\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}pdf
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Exploring Available Content}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/quickstart:exploring-available-content}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Before converting, you might want to see what’s available:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} List available JSON files}
5e2pdf\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }files

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} List loaded content by type}
5e2pdf\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }content\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }spell\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}limit\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+m}{10}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Search for specific content}
5e2pdf\PYG{+w}{ }list\PYG{+w}{ }content\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}search\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}fireball\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Show information about a specific item}
5e2pdf\PYG{+w}{ }info\PYG{+w}{ }content\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Fireball\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Converting Adventures}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/quickstart:converting-adventures}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Adventures are the most complex content type and have dedicated commands:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert an adventure to LaTeX}
5e2pdf\PYG{+w}{ }convert\PYG{+w}{ }adventure\PYG{+w}{ }adventure\PYGZhy{}cos.json

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Specify output location and include images}
5e2pdf\PYG{+w}{ }convert\PYG{+w}{ }adventure\PYG{+w}{ }adventure\PYGZhy{}cos.json\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}output\PYG{+w}{ }./output/cos.tex\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}images\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}title\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Curse of Strahd\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert and compile to PDF}
5e2pdf\PYG{+w}{ }convert\PYG{+w}{ }adventure\PYG{+w}{ }adventure\PYGZhy{}cos.json\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}pdf
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Converting Books}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/quickstart:converting-books}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Sourcebooks can be converted similarly:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert a sourcebook}
5e2pdf\PYG{+w}{ }convert\PYG{+w}{ }book\PYG{+w}{ }phb.json\PYG{+w}{ }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}output\PYG{+w}{ }phb.tex

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Include index and images}
5e2pdf\PYG{+w}{ }convert\PYG{+w}{ }book\PYG{+w}{ }phb.json\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}images\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}index\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}title\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}Player\PYGZsq{}s Handbook\PYGZdq{}}
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Converting Supplements}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/quickstart:converting-supplements}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For miscellaneous content like spell lists or creature collections:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert all content types}
5e2pdf\PYG{+w}{ }convert\PYG{+w}{ }supplement\PYG{+w}{ }spells\PYGZhy{}phb.json

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} Convert only specific content types}

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }spell\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}type\PYG{+w}{ }item

\label{\detokenize{user-guide/quickstart:legacy-mode}}

5e2pdf generates LaTeX files that you can:

\subsection{Configuration Tips}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/quickstart:configuration-tips}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
For frequently used options, create a configuration file:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} \PYGZti{}/.config/5e2pdf/config.yaml}
\PYG{n+nt}{output}\PYG{p}{:}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{default\PYGZus{}directory}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}\PYG{l+s}{./output}\PYG{l+s}{\PYGZdq{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{n+nt}{include\PYGZus{}images}\PYG{p}{:}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+lScalar+lScalarPlain}{true}

\PYG{n+nt}{latex}\PYG{p}{:}

\end{sphinxVerbatim}

Then your commands become simpler:

\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Common Workflows}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/quickstart:common-workflows}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Adventure Publishing Workflow}:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 1. Convert adventure with all features}

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}images\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}items\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}creatures\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+se}{\PYGZbs{}\PYGZbs{}}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}title\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{l+s+s2}{\PYGZdq{}My Custom Adventure\PYGZdq{}}

\PYG{c+c1}{\PYGZsh{} 2. Compile to PDF}

\sphinxAtStartPar

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {}

\subsection{Output Files}
\label{\detokenize{user-guide/cli-reference:output-files}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
5e2pdf generates LaTeX files with the following characteristics:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{UTF\sphinxhyphen{}8 encoding}: Full Unicode support for D\&D content

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{XeLaTeX compatible}: Optimized for XeLaTeX compilation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Modular structure}: Easy to include in larger documents

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{D\&D styling}: Matches official book formatting

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
To compile the generated LaTeX:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
xelatex\PYG{+w}{ }output.tex
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\PYG{+w}{  }\PYG{k}{while}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{read}\PYG{+w}{ }spell\PYG{p}{;}\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{k}{do}

\section{Architecture Overview}
\label{\detokenize{developer/architecture:architecture-overview}}\label{\detokenize{developer/architecture::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This document provides a high\sphinxhyphen{}level overview of the 5e2pdf architecture and design principles.


\subsection{System Overview}
\label{\detokenize{developer/architecture:system-overview}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
5e2pdf follows a modular, layered architecture designed for extensibility and maintainability:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    CLI Layer (Typer)                       │
│  ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐           │
│  │   Convert   │ │    List     │ │    Info     │  ...      │
│  └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  Application Layer                          │
│  ┌─────────────────────────────┐ ┌─────────────────────────┐ │
│  │     Rendering System        │ │    Content System       │ │
│  │  ┌─────────┐ ┌────────────┐ │ │ ┌─────────┐ ┌─────────┐ │ │
│  │  │ LaTeX   │ │  Template  │ │ │ │ Omnidx  │ │   Tag   │ │ │
│  │  │Renderer │ │  System    │ │ │ │ System  │ │Resolver │ │ │
│  │  └─────────┘ └────────────┘ │ │ └─────────┘ └─────────┘ │ │
│  └─────────────────────────────┘ └─────────────────────────┘ │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Core Layer                              │
│  ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐ ┌─────────────┐           │
│  │    Models   │ │   Loaders   │ │    Cache    │  ...      │
│  │ (Pydantic)  │ │    (JSON)   │ │   System    │           │
│  └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘ └─────────────┘           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                     Data Layer                              │
│           5etools JSON Data + User Content                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
\end{sphinxVerbatim}


\subsection{Core Components}
\label{\detokenize{developer/architecture:core-components}}

\subsubsection{Data Models (src/core/models/)}
\label{\detokenize{developer/architecture:data-models-src-core-models}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Built using Pydantic for robust data validation and serialization:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Content Models}: Spell, Creature, Item, Adventure, Book

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Base Types}: ContentType, Source, ContentItem

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Validation}: Automatic JSON validation with helpful error messages

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Type Safety}: Full type hints and runtime validation

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Key Features:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Flexible field handling for varying 5etools JSON structures

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Computed properties for formatted output

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Source tracking and validation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Cross\sphinxhyphen{}reference support

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Omnidexer System (src/core/loaders/)}
\label{\detokenize{developer/architecture:omnidexer-system-src-core-loaders}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The omnidexer is the central content management system:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Async Loading}: Parallel loading of JSON files for performance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Content Indexing}: Fast lookup by name, type, and source

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Cross\sphinxhyphen{}Reference Resolution}: Links between content items

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Caching}: Intelligent caching of loaded content

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Components:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{Omnidexer}}: Main coordinator class

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{JSONLoader}}: Handles JSON file parsing and validation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{SourceManager}}: Manages source book metadata

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Tag Resolution System (src/core/indexer/)}
\label{\detokenize{developer/architecture:tag-resolution-system-src-core-indexer}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Handles inline references and cross\sphinxhyphen{}links in D\&D content:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Tag Parsing}: Extracts \sphinxcode{\sphinxupquote{\{@spell fireball\}}} style tags

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Reference Resolution}: Finds target content items

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{LaTeX Generation}: Converts tags to appropriate LaTeX commands

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Fallback Handling}: Graceful handling of missing references

\end{itemize}

Abstract framework for document generation:

\sphinxAtStartPar

\item {}

\item {}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Concrete LaTeX document generation:

\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Document Structure}: Handles preamble, body, and postamble

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Content Renderers}: Specialized rendering for each content type

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Template Management}: LaTeX template system with inheritance

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Style Integration}: D\&D\sphinxhyphen{}style formatting and layout

Built using Typer for modern CLI development:

Backwards compatibility layer:

\subsection{Design Principles}
\label{\detokenize{developer/architecture:design-principles}}

\subsubsection{Modularity}
\label{\detokenize{developer/architecture:modularity}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Each component has a single, well\sphinxhyphen{}defined responsibility:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Models handle data validation and representation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Loaders manage data acquisition and parsing

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Renderers handle output generation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
CLI provides user interface

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
This allows for:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Easy testing of individual components

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pluggable architectures (e.g., different output formats)

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Clear separation of concerns

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Async\sphinxhyphen{}First Design}
\label{\detokenize{developer/architecture:async-first-design}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Heavy operations use async/await for performance:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Parallel JSON file loading

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Non\sphinxhyphen{}blocking I/O operations

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Responsive CLI during long operations

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Type Safety}
\label{\detokenize{developer/architecture:type-safety}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Comprehensive type hints throughout:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Pydantic models for runtime validation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
mypy compatibility for static analysis

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
IDE support with full autocomplete

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Caching Strategy}
\label{\detokenize{developer/architecture:caching-strategy}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Multi\sphinxhyphen{}level caching for performance:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Memory Cache}: In\sphinxhyphen{}process caching of loaded content

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Disk Cache}: Persistent caching of processed data

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Smart Invalidation}: Cache invalidation based on file timestamps

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Error Handling}
\label{\detokenize{developer/architecture:error-handling}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
Graceful error handling at all levels:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Validation Errors}: Clear messages for malformed JSON

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Missing Content}: Fallbacks for broken references

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{System Errors}: User\sphinxhyphen{}friendly error reporting

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Performance Considerations}
\label{\detokenize{developer/architecture:performance-considerations}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The system is designed for performance at scale:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Lazy Loading}: Content loaded only when needed

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Parallel Processing}: Multiple files processed simultaneously

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Efficient Indexing}: Fast lookups using Python dictionaries

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Caching}: Multiple levels of caching to avoid repeated work

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Memory usage is managed through:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Streaming}: Large files processed in chunks

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Weak References}: Automatic cleanup of unused content

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Cache Limits}: Configurable cache size limits

\end{itemize}

\subsection{Testing Philosophy}

5e2pdf follows a multi\sphinxhyphen{}layered testing approach:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Unit Tests}: Test individual components in isolation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Integration Tests}: Test component interactions

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{End\sphinxhyphen{}to\sphinxhyphen{}End Tests}: Test complete workflows

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Performance Tests}: Ensure acceptable performance characteristics

\end{itemize}

\section{Legacy System Documentation}
\label{\detokenize{developer/legacy:legacy-system-documentation}}\label{\detokenize{developer/legacy::doc}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
This document explains the legacy json2tex system and how it integrates with the modern 5e2pdf architecture.


\subsection{Historical Context}
\label{\detokenize{developer/legacy:historical-context}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The original json2tex.py script was created to convert 5etools JSON data directly to LaTeX. While functional, it had several limitations:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Monolithic design with tight coupling

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Limited extensibility for new content types

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
No proper error handling or validation

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Difficult to test and maintain

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
Command\sphinxhyphen{}line interface was basic

\end{itemize}

\sphinxAtStartPar
The modern 5e2pdf system addresses these issues while maintaining backwards compatibility.


\subsection{Legacy System Architecture}
\label{\detokenize{developer/legacy:legacy-system-architecture}}

\subsubsection{Original json2tex.py Structure}
\label{\detokenize{developer/legacy:original-json2tex-py-structure}}
\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
json2tex.py (single file)
├── Global variables and constants
├── JSON loading functions
├── Content parsing functions
├── LaTeX generation functions
├── Tag resolution (basic)
└── Main CLI logic
\end{sphinxVerbatim}

\sphinxAtStartPar
Key Components:
\begin{itemize}
\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Direct JSON parsing}: No validation or type safety

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Inline LaTeX generation}: Mixed logic and output

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Basic tag resolution}: Limited cross\sphinxhyphen{}referencing

\item {} 
\sphinxAtStartPar
\sphinxstylestrong{Procedural design}: No object\sphinxhyphen{}oriented structure

\end{itemize}


\subsubsection{Legacy Command\sphinxhyphen{}Line Interface}
\label{\detokenize{developer/legacy:legacy-command-line-interface}}
\sphinxAtStartPar
The original interface used simple flags:

\begin{sphinxVerbatim}[commandchars=\\\{\}]
python\PYG{+w}{ }json2tex.py\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{[}OPTIONS\PYG{o}{]}\PYG{+w}{ }INPUT\PYGZus{}FILE

Options:
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}adventure\PYG{+w}{          }Process\PYG{+w}{ }as\PYG{+w}{ }adventure
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}book\PYG{+w}{              }Process\PYG{+w}{ }as\PYG{+w}{ }book
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}supplement\PYG{+w}{        }Process\PYG{+w}{ }as\PYG{+w}{ }supplement
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}with\PYGZhy{}images\PYG{+w}{       }Include\PYG{+w}{ }images
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}no\PYGZhy{}images\PYG{+w}{         }Exclude\PYG{+w}{ }images\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{o}{(}default\PYG{o}{)}
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}add\PYGZhy{}items\PYG{+w}{         }Include\PYG{+w}{ }item\PYG{+w}{ }appendices
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}no\PYGZhy{}items\PYG{+w}{          }Exclude\PYG{+w}{ }item\PYG{+w}{ }appendices
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}add\PYGZhy{}creatures\PYG{+w}{     }Include\PYG{+w}{ }creature\PYG{+w}{ }appendices
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}no\PYGZhy{}creatures\PYG{+w}{      }Exclude\PYG{+w}{ }creature\PYG{+w}{ }appendices
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}help\PYG{+w}{              }Show\PYG{+w}{ }\PYG{n+nb}{help}\PYG{+w}{ }message
\PYG{+w}{  }\PYGZhy{}\PYGZhy{}version\PYG{+w}{           }Show\PYG{+w}{ }version
\end{sphinxVerbatim}
